---
title: "Installation"
---

## Prerequisites

- Python 3.10 or newer.
- Node.js 18 or newer, required for the web frontend.
- Arduino IDE or `arduino-cli`, required for flashing the Teensy firmware.
- A serial-capable machine (Linux, macOS, or Windows with a USB-serial driver).

## Clone the repository

```bash
git clone https://github.com/anishgoyal1108/Reactive-Robot.git
cd Reactive-Robot
```

## Python environment

```bash
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate              # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r braccio_main_runner/requirements.txt
pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
```

`requirements.txt` pulls in `pyserial`, `pybullet`, `pybullet-planning`, `py-trees`, `scipy`, `fastapi`, `uvicorn`, `pydantic`, `lark`, `numpy`, and `matplotlib`. `requirements-dev.txt` adds `mypy`, `pytest`, `httpx`, `quartodoc`, and `griffe` for type-checking, tests, and wiki generation.

## Firmware

1. Flash the stock Braccio firmware to the Arduino Mega from the Arduino IDE.
2. Open `ToF_RR_Sensing/arduino/vl5_tca_4x4/vl5_tca_4x4/vl5_tca_4x4.ino` and flash to the Teensy 4.1.

The Teensy firmware reads four VL53L5CX sensors on a TCA9548A I2C mux, four IR sensors through a NOR-inverter stage on pins 23, 22, 21, 20, and an MPU-6050 IMU. See the [wiring reference](../hardware/wiring.qmd) for the pin map.

## Web frontend

```bash
cd web/frontend
npm install
```

The frontend is a Vite + React + Blockly SPA. `npm run dev` starts a dev server on port 5173 with a proxy to the FastAPI backend; `npm run build` produces a static bundle under `dist/`.

## Verify the install

Run the controller against the digital twin to confirm every dependency resolves:

```bash
python -m braccio_twin
```

The process should print a PyBullet banner and the safety stack initialization log, then hold at the sim main loop. Press Ctrl+C to exit.
